result:
task: Regenerate `.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md` with rulesync for W2-52 (DAEO-siiz), copy it into the worktree, verify, commit it, run the builder tests and clean up.
status: PACKAGES — rulesync ran and showed that only the adopt skill is stale, but copying it into the worktree was refused twice (once combined, once alone). Under AR-6 I stopped there, so nothing was committed.
work_completed: All the start checks matched: `engineer` / `DAEO-siiz`, `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52`, `w2/W2-52`, HEAD `d1ba2dfd2054`. I made `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-52/tmp.vpTHSVuhUS` and ran rulesync 24.0.0 there with the given command; it wrote 34 files. I compared each one with `cmp` against the worktree, leaving out `.claude/settings.json`, which I neither read nor compared. Exactly one file differs: `.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md`. I looked at the diff (14 lines): the generated copy rewrites the "Independent gates" section for the lite A7 and A10 stages (CAP-44.f, DEC-741, CAP-44.h, CAP-44.k). That matches the ticket title, so nothing suggests the source is wrong. Steps 3, 5 and 6 (copy, commit, builder tests) were not done because of the refusal, and step 7 (removing the temp folder) was refused too.
files_changed: none. `git status --short` and `git diff --stat` are both empty and HEAD is still `d1ba2dfd2054`.
evidence: `gov.__file__` prints `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/src/gov/__init__.py`. The portability check ran on the unchanged tree because the copy was refused alongside it. It gave one finding, `{"code": "GENERATED_DIFFERS", "message": "is not what rulesync generates from its sources", "file": ".claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md"}`, its `compared` block was `{"rulesync_version": true, "kernel_files": 29, "generated_files": 44}`, and it exited 1. That confirms the stale file but is not the passing run the task asks for. The two refusals for the copy: (1) the call `cp … && cmp …` got "This Bash command contains multiple operations. The following parts require approval: cp …, cmp …"; (2) `cp` alone got "Claude requested permissions to edit /tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-52/tmp.vpTHSVuhUS/.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md which is a sensitive file." There is no commit, so there is no hash or trailer block.
tests: none run. The builder tests (`tests/unit/adopt`) are step 6, after the commit, and I stopped before that. No acceptance suite was run.
discoveries: The Claude Code permission layer, not the gov guard, treats any path containing `.claude/` as sensitive. That includes rulesync's output folder under `/tmp`, so both copying from it and deleting it need explicit approval in this non-interactive session. Starting outside the sandbox removes the read-only mount but not this approval gate. Apart from the adopt skill and the uncompared `.claude/settings.json`, rulesync would change no other file (43 files identical, none missing).
risks: My temp folder `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-52/tmp.vpTHSVuhUS` is still there because `rm -r` was refused twice (once combined with `ls`, once alone). It holds 460K and 68 files and folders, well inside the 2 GB / 50,000 share. It contains a generated `.claude/settings.json`, which I did not read. The worktree is untouched.
lessons: The next engineer needs approval, set up in advance, for the exact `cp` into `.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md` and for `rm -r` of its own temp folder; otherwise it hits the same wall at step 3. The rulesync step and the comparison work without any approval.
proposed_decisions: Package P1, how the one write into `.claude/` is approved. The question is how to let this single prescribed write through. Why now: it is the ticket's whole change, and W2-52 cannot close without it. Option (a): relaunch the engineer with session-level allow rules, passed in `--settings` at launch and not in the committed `.claude/settings.json`, for exactly `Bash(cp /tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-52/<dir>/.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/.claude/skills/adopt/SKILL.md)` and `rm -r` of its own temp folder. If an allow rule does not override the sensitive-path check, a permission mode that does would be needed. Option (b): run the engineer interactively so the owner approves the one prompt. Option (c): the lead or owner does the single `cp` by hand and the engineer then verifies and commits. Impact: one generated file; no source, test or other generated file changes. Reversibility: fully reversible (one commit on `w2/W2-52`, not merged). Cost: one more engineer session of a few minutes. Recommendation: (a), because it keeps the change to the engineer role and stays scoped to the exact command. Confidence: medium, since I have not confirmed whether an allow rule alone gets past the `.claude/` sensitive-file check in this Claude Code version.
unresolved: The adopt skill's generated copy is still stale and the portability check still exits 1. There is no commit and the builder tests have not run. The temp folder `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-52/tmp.vpTHSVuhUS` has not been removed (460K, 68 files and folders). Permission refusals: the copy twice and `rm -r` twice; I stopped after the second refusal each time. Read refusals from the guard: 0. I did not use `gov retrieve`; the task was mechanical.
recommended_next_action: Decide P1, then relaunch an engineer with the exact `cp` and temp-folder `rm -r` approved, so it can copy, verify, commit and run `tests/unit/adopt`; the lead or engineer also removes the leftover temp folder.
